kanban_add_note.description: Adds a short note to a ticket (1000 characters max): a decision, a fact found, an answer of the user worth keeping. Not for progress logs, restatements of the ticket or corrections of earlier notes.

id.description: Ticket number (default: the ticket of the worktree you are in)

kanban_create.description: Creates a ticket in the backlog (status New). Use it when the user asks for it or agrees to note a task for later.

depends_on.description: Tickets of other lineages this one waits for: it starts once they are merged or done (replaces the list)

description.description: Description in Markdown, 1500 characters max: context, need, acceptance criteria

files.description: Paths of the files concerned (relative to the root of the project)

milestone.description: Milestone of the ticket and of its steps (0 takes it out; a step has the one of its root); see kanban_milestone

objective.description: Objective of the ticket and of its steps, apart from its milestone (0 takes it out; a step has the one of its root); see kanban_objective

parent.description: Root ticket: this one becomes a step of its lineage, developed in the root's worktree after the previous steps (0 takes it out). Only before its development starts

kanban_feedback.description: Test feedback of a ticket: add one (a bug, a missing feature or an info found while testing), mark one handled (done) once fixed and verified, or open again (reopen).

complexity.description: How hard the fix is (add): low, medium or high; it picks the model of the fix session

id.description: Ticket number (default: the ticket of the worktree you are in)

kanban_get.description: Reads a whole ticket: description, notes, plan, goals and test feedback (with their ids), linked files, conversations, branch and worktree.

id.description: Ticket number (default: the ticket of the worktree you are in)

kanban_goal.description: Checks, unchecks, adds, edits or deletes a goal of a ticket. Check each goal as soon as it is reached and verified.

description.description: How to check it (add, edit; optional)

goal.description: Goal id (check, uncheck, edit, delete), see kanban_get

id.description: Ticket number (default: the ticket of the worktree you are in)

kanban_list.description: Lists the tickets of the kanban of the project (number, status, priority, title, goals, open feedback).

status.description: Status filter (optional; review is the old name of to_test)

kanban_milestone.description: Milestones group the tickets of one feature (across lineages) with its spec, user stories and feedback; the user validates them. Actions: list; get (id); create (title, description, spec); update (id; title, description, spec, objective); story_add (id, text: "As a <user>, I <can do>…"), story_edit (id, story, text), story_delete (id, story); feedback_add (id, kind, text, complexity), feedback_done / feedback_reopen (id, feedback); note (id, text: a decision). Only the user validates a story or a milestone. Put a ticket in a milestone with the milestone field of kanban_create / kanban_update.

complexity.description: How hard handling the feedback is (feedback_add)

description.description: Description in Markdown, 1500 characters max: the feature, its scope (create, update)

id.description: Milestone number (all actions but list and create)

objective.description: Default objective of the milestone; its open tickets go into it (update; 0: none); see kanban_objective

spec.description: The spec: a path of the repository or an address (create, update)

text.description: User story (500 characters max), feedback or note (1000 characters max)

kanban_move.description: Moves a ticket from In progress to To test (status to_test), with test_summary: how to test it. Other changes of status belong to the user.

id.description: Ticket number (default: the ticket of the worktree you are in)

status.description: New status (review is the old name of to_test)

test_summary.description: What to test and how (steps, commands, expected results), in Markdown

kanban_objective.description: Objectives are named deadlines (MVP, a launch…) in order: a milestone says what (one feature), an objective says when, taking tickets of several milestones and lone ones. A ticket has one objective at most, apart from its milestone. Actions: list (in order); get (id: its tickets grouped by milestone); create (title, description, due); update (id; title, description, due); note (id, text: a decision). Only the user reaches, abandons or reorders an objective. Put a ticket in an objective with the objective field of kanban_create / kanban_update, a milestone's open tickets with the objective field of kanban_milestone update.

description.description: Description in Markdown, 1500 characters max: what reaching it means (create, update)

due.description: Date aimed at, YYYY-MM-DD; empty: none (create, update)

kanban_set_plan.description: Writes the implementation plan of a ticket and its goals (verifiable objectives, checked during development). Replaces the plan and the goals of a previous plan (the goals of the user stay). A New ticket moves to "To do".

complexity.description: How hard the work is, which picks the model and the effort of its sessions: low (a small obvious change: a color, a label, a one-line fix), medium (usual work), high (a delicate design, concurrency, security, a bug hard to find)

description.description: How to check it (optional, a few lines)

id.description: Ticket number (default: the ticket of the worktree you are in)

plan.description: Plan in Markdown: approach, files, steps, risks, tests

size.description: Estimated effort of the whole ticket: s (a few files, an hour of AI work), m, l, xl (many files across the pod and the page, several days)

kanban_start.description: Starts the development of a ticket ("To do", or "In progress" / "To test" without a worktree): creates the branch ticket/<n>-<slug> from the base in a worktree of the project, runs the setup commands of the project there (its saved commands flagged setup), and moves the ticket to "In progress". Answers the worktree: work there, with absolute paths, and commit on that branch.

base.description: Base branch (optional: the base of the ticket or of the kanban, else origin/main or main)

id.description: Ticket number (default: the ticket of the worktree you are in)

kanban_update.description: Changes a ticket (only the given fields).

complexity.description: How hard the work is, which picks the model and the effort of its sessions: low (a small obvious change: a color, a label, a one-line fix), medium (usual work), high (a delicate design, concurrency, security, a bug hard to find)

depends_on.description: Tickets of other lineages this one waits for: it starts once they are merged or done (replaces the list)

id.description: Ticket number (default: the ticket of the worktree you are in)

milestone.description: Milestone of the ticket and of its steps (0 takes it out; a step has the one of its root); see kanban_milestone

objective.description: Objective of the ticket and of its steps, apart from its milestone (0 takes it out; a step has the one of its root); see kanban_objective

parent.description: Root ticket: this one becomes a step of its lineage, developed in the root's worktree after the previous steps (0 takes it out). Only before its development starts

size.description: Estimated effort of the whole ticket: s (a few files, an hour of AI work), m, l, xl (many files across the pod and the page, several days)

test_summary.description: How to test the ticket (Markdown): steps, commands, expected results
